description:
A complete 87-piece service for 12 in Noritake Ivory China’s Parkridge pattern (No. 7561). Each piece has a warm ivory body and a graceful border of sage green scrolls and leafy sprigs with clusters of tiny white flowers. A fine platinum band sits inside the border, and a platinum trim finishes every rim. The set includes dinner plates, salad plates, bread and butter plates, rimmed soup bowls, fruit or dessert bowls, teacups with saucers, a creamer, an open sugar bowl, and a gravy boat with an attached underplate. It would suit holiday dinners and formal entertaining, a wedding or anniversary table, or replacing pieces in a Parkridge collection.

Pieces: 12 dinner plates, 12 salad plates, 12 bread and butter plates, 12 rimmed soup bowls, 12 fruit or dessert bowls, 12 teacups, 12 saucers, 1 creamer, 1 open sugar bowl, and 1 gravy boat with attached underplate (87 pieces)

Marks: Backstamp reads “Noritake Ivory China, Japan, 7561, Parkridge” with the laurel wreath “N” logo

Classic estate smoking pipe crafted from imported briar wood, featuring decorative diagonal carved fluting across the bowl and distinct stamping along the shank. IN THE SAME CONDITION AS THEY WERE RECEIVED

Refunds for shipping damages are not issued until the FedEx claim is finalized and approved

It is not advised to contact us over the phone regarding customer service matters; we can best and most quickly assist you here through the Customer Service Portal. description:
Natural Mineral Specimen Lot of 2
Amethyst Quartz Cluster & Cut Base Green Fluorite
2 Pieces
This lot of two natural geological specimens features an amethyst quartz crystal geode cluster and a substantial rough green fluorite display piece with a sawn flat base. The amethyst specimen exhibits lavender to violet crystalline points resting atop a layered agate and basalt matrix band. The companion green fluorite specimen displays pale seafoam to emerald-green translucent crystalline mass with natural rough cleavage and mineral veining, cut flat on the bottom and back for upright shelf or tabletop display.
Includes two distinct natural mineral display specimens
Amethyst cluster features defined crystalline druzy terminations and agate banding
Green fluorite specimen features cut flat base and back for stable freestanding display
Suitable for mineral collectors, lapidary display, or natural interior accents
Condition:
Very good natural condition. Amethyst points are largely intact with minor natural edge wear and matrix inclusions. Green fluorite shows natural crystalline cleavage planes, internal fractures, and rough matrix crust consistent with natural raw stone.

Raw Earth-Mined Crystals, Points & Rough Chunks
Total Weight: 6.4 lbs
This natural mineral collection features a diverse assortment of quartz specimens totaling approximately 6.4 pounds. Centered around a substantial raw rose quartz rough piece displaying delicate pink coloration and natural crystalline fracturing, the collection also includes an array of clear quartz points, clusters, and raw fragments. Valued by mineral collectors, lapidary crafters, and crystal enthusiasts, these pieces highlight the distinctive geometry and natural clarity characteristic of quartz minerals.
Prominent rough rose quartz specimen measuring approximately 4.5 inches across
Clear quartz crystal points with visible terminations and prismatic striations
Assorted crystalline clusters, rough chunks, and smaller crystal shards
Total collection weight of 6.4 pounds

description: 11L x 7W x 17H.  No cord. Not tested. For restoration project or home decor purposes. This vintage Silvertone Superheterodyne portable radio was manufactured by Victor Company in Camden, N.J., U.S.A. Model 280591-1. It features RCA tube components inside, including glass vacuum tubes with Silvertone and RCA markings visible through the back panel opening. The radio has a black textured exterior with metal control knobs for volume and station selection. The front includes a three-section cloth speaker grille. The top of the unit has a black leather carrying handle attached with metal hardware. The radio shows visible wear, scuffs, and some rust on metal parts consistent with its age. It is a collectible piece likely from the early-to-mid 20th century and is in used, unrestored condition.

This listing includes a collection of rough rock salt mineral specimens, often mistaken for rose quartz due to their pink hues. The stones are unpolished and vary in size and shape, exhibiting natural pink colors with occasional white and reddish-brown inclusions. The material is translucent with a crystalline structure. Mixing Flat-Rate & Dimensional Weight Items
When an order includes both flat-rate and dimensional-weight items, shipping may be calculated using dimensional weight. Combining these items does not necessarily reduce shipping costs and may result in the same or higher shipping charges than purchasing them separately.
For this reason, customers may want to consider purchasing flat-rate and dimensional-weight items in separate orders.

.

FedEx cannot ship to a Military Box, PO Box, or Puerto Rico. Orders with a tracking number assigned on a weekend are picked up by the carrier on Monday afternoon. Any order with items totaling $300 or more will automatically require a signature.

Bring a touch of natural wonder to your collection with this set of two medium-sized geodes. Each geode features a striking contrast between a rough stone exterior and sparkling crystal-lined interiors, revealed beautifully when split open. The raw, earthy exterior is typical for naturally formed geodes, while each center showcases mineral crystals that reflect the light, adding a captivating sparkle and depth to their natural design. Perfect for mineral collectors, crystal enthusiasts, or those who appreciate unique natural decor, these geodes offer visual interest and timeless appeal. Their sturdy stone composition ensures long-lasting beauty and durability, whether displayed as conversation pieces or used in educational settings to demonstrate natural geological processes. Both pieces show some typical surface weathering on the exterior, with intact and undamaged crystal interiors. There are no visible cracks or repairs. Ideal for display as-is or for use in rock and mineral studies. The set consists of two separate geodes, each with its own distinct crystal pattern and coloration

description:
Art Glass Cullet Chunk
Cobalt Blue with Rainbow Iridescent Finish
Decorative Glass Specimen, 1.365 Pounds
Substantial decorative chunk of cobalt blue cullet slag glass displaying a vibrant iridescent carnival-style flash across fractured planes and smooth surfaces. Raw glass chunks like this were produced during the glassmaking process at heritage American glassworks, where excess furnace glass cooled into monolithic blocks before being fractured into decorative specimens prized for garden displays, lapidary projects, and paperweights.
Intense translucent cobalt blue glass body with rich color depth
Exterior exhibits strong rainbow iridescence in vivid hues of gold, magenta, and turquoise
Natural conchoidal fracturing showcasing glass cleavage, smooth waves, and raw crystalline textures
Measures approximately 4 inches by 2.25 inches by 3.25 inches; weighs 1.365 pounds
Condition:
Formed as a raw fractured glass chunk with natural sharp edges, conchoidal ridges, and cleavage faces inherent to slag glass. Clean surfaces with brilliant luster and no post-manufacture cloudiness or chemical damage.

title: Hemingray 42 Glass Insulator Set 2 Aqua Blue Green CD 154 Made in USA Vintage
description:
Hemingray Glass Company Set - 2 Pieces
Hemingray 42 (CD 154)
Aqua, Vintage Mid-Century
This set features two vintage aqua glass insulators produced by the Hemingray Glass Company, identified by the "Hemingray-42" mold mark. The No. 42 model, classified as CD 154 by collectors, was one of the most widely used designs for telephone and telegraph lines across North America during the early-to-mid 20th century. Prized for their deep aqua color and iconic industrial aesthetic, these pieces represent a significant era of American telecommunications history and are staple items for glass insulator collectors.
Pieces Included:
Glass Insulator, Hemingray 42, Aqua, Beaded Base - minor fleabites on drip points
Glass Insulator, Hemingray 42, Aqua, Beaded Base - minor fleabites on drip points
Condition:
Both insulators are in good vintage condition with characteristic wear expected from outdoor utility use. The glass retains high clarity and its original vibrant aqua hue. As is common with authentic vintage insulators, there are minor fleabites and small chips along the sharp drip points on the beaded base. No large structural cracks or major damage to the wire grooves or top domes observed.
